title: Business analyst
change: Occupational standard and assessment plan revised
overviewOfRole: Working with organisations to improve their information systems.

knowledges.detail: The definition of Business Analysis and the range of activities that constitute it, along with its value in enabling business improvement and delivering digital change.
The role of the Business Analyst, and its relationship with other roles on a business change initiative, and how the business analysis work contributes to the organisational objectives.

Business change and system development life cycles (such as waterfall and agile), how organisational context influences the choice of delivery approach and the differences between linear, incremental and iterative methodologies.
The importance of effective communication and engagement with a range of internal and external stakeholders in relation to Business Analysis activities.

Technology and industry trends across the digital sector, and the opportunities these bring for business improvement, considering the ethical implications and limitations of emerging technologies including Artificial Intelligence.
The role of software and AI tools in improving the efficiency and quality of business analysis work.
Legislation and industry standards relevant to the organisation and sector, including data protection regulations
Approaches to conducting situational analysis e.g. SWOT and PESTLE analysis and other approaches suitable for the organisational context.

Investigative and requirements‑elicitation techniques, including their advantages, disadvantages and the situations in which each is most effective. This includes qualitative methods (e.g. interviews, workshops, prototypes), quantitative approaches (e.g. surveys, data analysis), and techniques that surface tacit knowledge (e.g. observation, shadowing).
The purpose and value of modelling business processes.
Different approaches to model business processes and the factors that influence the choice of modelling technique such as swimlane diagrams, activity diagrams and customer journeys.

The importance of considering user experience, accessibility (including  frameworks for inclusive design for those with disabilities and/or health conditions) and usability requirements in the design of digital solutions.
Approaches to categorise, validate, prioritise and manage requirements throughout the lifecycle, including the role of change control in maintaining requirements integrity.
The value of data to an organisation, and how data needs are considered in business improvement.

Data modelling techniques, standards, notation and software tools that enable business analysts to develop simple data models (e.g class models, entity relationship diagrams, data flow diagrams) that support analysis, design and decision‑making.
The purpose and activities of the gap analysis process.
The role of the business analyst in facilitating business acceptance of changes, including business change readiness, user acceptance testing and system deployment.
The purpose and importance of business change impact assessment.
The concepts of benefits realisation and management.

behaviours.detail: Act logically, analytically, ethically, and objectively in a range of situations.
Demonstrate curiosity when problem solving by asking questions, seeking ideas and thinking creatively.
Work collaboratively as a Business Analyst to build and maintain positive working relationships with people from technical and non-technical backgrounds.
Use own initiative and take responsibility appropriate to the role of Business Analyst.
Work flexibly and effectively as a Business Analyst in a multidisciplinary team.
Demonstrate commitment to continuous professional development in relation to Business Analysis and the digital sector.

skills.detail: Scope and plan Business Analysis activities and outputs.
Communicate effectively in a variety of business analysis situations with a range of stakeholders, presenting information in a manner appropriate to the audience.
Plan and facilitate structured group discussions or workshops to enable stakeholders to collaborate effectively, share insights and reach clear outcomes.
Apply structured investigation techniques to define a business situation and identify its problems and opportunities.
Apply business analysis techniques to analyse and document options and recommendations for change
Support the identification and presentation of proposals to stakeholders to gain agreement.
Elicit process information from stakeholders.

Model business processes for the current (as is) and proposed (to be) using relevant standards, notation (such as UML and BPMN) software tools and techniques for example, swimlane diagrams, activity diagrams and customer journeys.
Analyse business process models to identify opportunities for improvement.
Elicit requirements from stakeholders to identify business and user needs.
Document clear functional and non-functional requirements in line with organisational standards.
Analyse requirements to identify and remove duplication, conflict, and overlap, and work with stakeholders to validate and prioritise them, using a structured approach.
Support the controlled management and traceability of requirements (horizontal and vertical) throughout the lifecycle.
Elicit business data needs from stakeholders and other sources (such as business documentation, existing systems and legislation).
Document current business situations to enable gap analysis and decision making.
Support the development of models of future state business situations (e.g. process models, data models, organisational design etc).
Identify key differences between current and future business situations and the actions required to move between the two.
Define acceptance criteria for business and system changes, and provide support to ensure business and user acceptance of these changes.
Apply and explain relevant techniques to research and identify stakeholders.
Analyse and document stakeholders and their areas of interest and influence and use this to determine the communication and engagement approach.
Support the development of cost-benefit analysis for proposed business changes.
Evaluate and document the key impacts on people, process, organisation, technology and information.

duties.dutyDetail: Communicate and collaborate with stakeholders to enable the analysis and delivery of technology and business change.
Apply structured techniques to investigate wants, needs, problems and opportunities.
Document the current situation and apply business analysis techniques to structure information.
Assist in the development of options and recommendations for change.
Model business processes using visual techniques.
Analyse business processes to identify, capture and agree process changes and improvements
Undertake requirements elicitation with stakeholders to identify business and user needs
Analyse, validate, prioritise, document, and support the controlled management of functional and non‑functional requirements to ensure they remain accurate, relevant, and aligned to business needs.
Identify data requirements relating to business improvement.
Compare current and future state business situations in order to identify the changes required for business improvement.
Define acceptance criteria for business and system changes, and support business acceptance.
Identify and analyse stakeholders impacted by a proposed change, understand their perspectives and assess how their interests are best managed.
Assess and document the drivers, costs, benefits and impacts of a proposed business change.
